HOW THE TREE WORKS

A decomposition of drivers, inspired by DuPont.

Each of the four branches has a 25% budget. Within a branch, importance weights are High = 3 and Medium = 2. Direction runs from −2 (strong bearish) to +2 (strong bullish). The total is 100 × Σ(branch weight × weighted direction / 2). Unrated factors contribute no directional evidence; their weight stays in the denominator. Coverage shows how much of the full tree you have rated.

Fed, yields and oil share one liquidity branch to limit double counting. This is an additive research model, not DuPont’s accounting identity. Its score is a subjective balance of factors, not a probability of a rally. The four budgets are assumptions, not calibrated forecasts.

The example reproduces the direction of your pasted claims as an unverified scenario. Source links are research starting points, not proof of those headlines. This page does not fetch news, prices, ETF flows or derivatives data. Your readings and notes remain local to this browser. Coin lenses change the interpretation, not the score; coin-specific evidence is still needed.
